takeaway: In a right hemicolectomy the right ureter, the right gonadal vessels and the second part of the duodenum are at risk.

question.text: In a right hemicolectomy, which structure is encountered during dissection?
question.say: When performing a right hemicolectomy, which of the following structures is encountered during dissection?

answer.say: The answer is the right ureter.

lines.text: Two surgeons lift the colon in a right hemicolectomy.
lines.say: Two surgeons lift the colon during a right hemicolectomy. Behind it lie important relations of the right colon.

lines.text: Underneath, the right ureter waves a red flag.
lines.say: Underneath, the right ureter waves a red flag. Watch the ureter!

lines.text: Next to it, the right gonadal vessels.
lines.say: Next to it lie the right gonadal vessels.

lines.text: And the second part of the duodenum.
lines.say: And nearby, the second part of the duodenum.

lines.text: These three structures are at risk and need careful identification.
lines.say: These three structures are at risk. Vigilance and careful identification are needed to prevent injury at the time of surgery.

lines.text: Remember: a right hemicolectomy puts the right ureter at risk.
lines.say: Remember: in a right hemicolectomy, find the right ureter.
